role: the test architect who has seen coverage lie
verdict: Not yet: the spec names more tests than most products ship and still lets green be produced without the property being observed, because the gate runs the code under review, a mutation stub is unconstrained, a removed invariant goes red nowhere after the one-time acceptance, and nothing counts or forbids what did not run.

findings.defect: S6's mutation check accepts any stub that makes a tagged test fail, one stub per invariant id, so the property can be unobserved while S6 is met.
findings.scenario: The mutate_I7 stub panics; every tagged I7 test goes red under it and tools/ci mutate passes; the preflight call missing from retire is observed by no test, and S6 is recorded as met.
findings.change: In 05 5.2 define a stub as a pass-through of the guarded decision (the guard admits what it refuses) and nothing else; require the red to come from a tagged test's own assertion; make the stub per guard site (mutate_I<n>_<site>) and require at least one tagged test red per site.
findings.cost: a paragraph in 05 5.2, a rule in tools/ci mutate, and one tag suffix per guard site; mutate runs longer

findings.defect: A guard deleted together with its test and both tags, as Boundaries requires, turns nothing red: invariants pairs what remains and acceptance runs once.
findings.scenario: A refactor PR removes a guard site, its test and the two tags in one commit after v1.0.0; tools/ci invariants finds no unpaired tag, all is green, and the row of 05 5.2 still claims the E-level test.
findings.change: Add to 05 5.2 and the invariants row of 10 10.2 a committed list of invariant ids expected in code, appended by tools/new invariant and never shortened without the approval line; invariants fails when a listed id has no guard or test tag in the code.
findings.cost: one data file on the checks surface, one clause in tools/ci invariants, two sentences

findings.defect: CI and the hook run the tools/ci of the branch under review, so a change to the gate is judged by itself, and no mechanism or deferred row names the gap.
findings.scenario: A PR edits tools/ci so that coverage passes and types its own approval line for the checks surface; ci.yml checks out the PR and runs its tools/ci all, which exits 0; the merge comes through the API with the operator's token (05 5.4).
findings.change: In 10 10.2 state that ci.yml runs the base branch's tools/ci against the merge result (a second checkout of base, go run from it), or add a row to the Deferred decisions table with the trigger (the first PR that touches tools/ci and a package it checks).
findings.cost: a decision; a few lines of workflow inside the grammar of 10 10.2, or one deferred row

findings.defect: S6 is evidenced by three tool names and no run; mutate is not a step of all and release.yml runs all, so the release commit never has a mutate result.
findings.scenario: The last mutate run is a scheduled fuzz.yml run on a commit three weeks before the tag; acceptance checks tags per row and records S6 as met for v1.0.0.
findings.change: Make the S6 Evidence cell a ci-run item of a mutate run on the tagged commit, and have release.yml call go run ./tools/ci mutate before tools/release build (10 10.2, Release and bootstrap).
findings.cost: one run step in release.yml, one evidence item, release time grows by the mutate run

postmortem: After v1.0.0, as L6 would see it fail. (1) An operator lost three days of unpushed work on romeu rm: the salvage bundle lacked a worktree branch created after the last snapshot; the I17 cases were green against a test git daemon and the fake sbx, and J6, the one journey that exercises --stop-agents against a live agent, ran once on the release candidate on one host; nothing in CI ever ran J6 (09; S7; 08 8.5; 10 10.1; 11 11.2). (2) A guard disappeared with its test and both tags in one commit, as Boundaries requires; tools/ci invariants paired what was left; acceptance had run once before the tag and never again (05 5.2; index Boundaries; 10 10.5). (3) S6 was true and meant nothing: the mutate_I7 stub panicked, every tagged test went red as asked, the one guard site with no observing test hid behind the forty that had one, and the release commit never had a mutate run because mutate is not in all (S6; 05 5.2; 10 10.2; 10 10.5). (4) The hybrid level stopped running on the arm64 runner for seven weeks after a runner image lost its Docker daemon: the step is selected inside tools/ci, 10 10.1 called the failure an infrastructure error and not a test failure, nothing counted the tests that ran, and I30 shipped broken for arm64 (10 10.1; 10 10.2; ADR 0007). (5) The gate was edited by the thing it gated: an agent lowered a coverage threshold inside tools/ci, typed the approval line for the checks surface, CI ran the PR's own tools/ci, and the merge came through the API with the operator's token (05 5.3; 05 5.4; 12 12.4; ADR 0008). (6) The S8 timing test flaked on a loaded runner and the bound was raised, so the view derivation that reads the whole ledger shipped at 9 s on a machine with a year of entries; the CI figure had always been measured on an empty ledger (S8; 10 10.1; index Deferred decisions). (7) Coverage was 83 percent and the tests asserted almost nothing: dark packages with author-written tests, a package with no test file absent from the profile, require.NoError everywhere (S9; 10 10.2; 12 12.9). (8) The forbidden-name matcher stopped matching after a refactor; the self-test ran on its own synthetic denylist and passed; a name reached a public PR title (10 10.2). (9) Not said aloud: the scheduled fuzz.yml was red for two months and nobody read it; t.Skip appeared in eleven tests under a GOOS check because nothing forbade it; the host suite did not compile for a sprint and block B found it after the candidate was tagged; the v1.0.0 binaries were never run in a sandbox, the RC binaries were, and the two were declared the same by argument from pins; the only reviewer of the test strategy's weak points is the account that writes the tests. The test plan is careful where it was already strong (13 13.10) and trusting where green is decided: who runs the gate, what a stub is, whether a skipped or unrun test is counted, and whether anything after the final task ever checks again (10 10.1; 10 10.2; 10 10.5; 11 11.2; 12 12.9; ADR 0007).
lens_critique: This lens measures success by whether a gate turns red, and for this product that is an instrument, not the goal: success is that no operator loses work and no agent code runs on the host. Three ways the lens misjudges here. It assumes an adversarial author and an independent reader of red; ADR 0008 makes author and reviewer one account, so a red that nobody is obliged to read is worth less than the lens prices it, and a mechanism that stops the merge (which the lens does not ask for) is worth more. It prefers mechanisms to judgment and would happily add expected-test manifests, per-site stubs and positive controls to a 102-task plan for one maintainer; each is right in isolation and together they can cost more than the loss they prevent, which the delivery lens and the scope skeptic should weigh against this report. And it treats once-run host evidence as weak, where for a product whose real behaviour exists only on a Mac with sbx, a well-recorded single run on both hosts is the strongest evidence available and the fake is the approximation; the lens should ask for the host run to be re-runnable and recorded rather than for CI to pretend to be the host.
